results.answer_markdown: **AEHR (Aehr Test Systems) sells semiconductor test and burn-in equipment to chip manufacturers, primarily for AI and data center applications.** ### FACTS - **What AEHR sells:** A portfolio of test and burn-in systems including FOX-CP, FOX-XP, FOX-NP (wafer-level), DiePak carriers (die-level), Sonoma and Tahoe systems (packaged-part burn-in), and associated consumables like WaferPak contactors and burn-in modules. These are used to stress-test semiconductors before final packaging. - **Who pays:** Semiconductor companies — foundries, IDMs, and OSATs. Recent demand is driven by AI and data center customers, per the press release. - **Business model:** Primarily capital equipment sales of test systems. The company may also generate revenue from consumable products such as carriers and contactors, though the press release does not detail a recurring revenue split. Service and support revenue is not confirmed in available evidence. - **Recent performance:** In fiscal Q1 2026 (ended Aug 29, 2025), net revenue was $11.0M (down from $13.1M year-over-year), GAAP net loss of $(2.1)M, and non-GAAP net income of $0.2M. Bookings were $11.4M, backlog $15.5M. ### GAPS - No customer list or revenue concentration data. - No explicit breakdown of equipment vs. consumables revenue or gross margins. - No 10-K or formal investor presentation retrieved; analysis relies on a single press release. - Not a financial firm — no lending, spread income, fee income, or carried interest to report. ### SOURCE REFS - Aehr Test Systems press release dated October 6, 2025: [Aehr.com](https://www.aehr.com/2025/10/aehr-test-systems-reports-fiscal-2026-first-quarter-financial-results/) - News articles from The Motley Fool and Yahoo Finance confirm the company's focus on semiconductor test and burn-in for AI/data centers.
